understand.title: Understand the Request
understand.instruction: Analyze the development request before proposing an implementation, using the Clear-Thought tools: run at least two sequential_thinking calls to structure the analysis (a single call is pointless — use the second to challenge or refine the first) and reference its conclusions in the submission. Provide a concise summary, assumptions, open questions, constraints, risks, measurable acceptance criteria, and affected areas. When the request names multiple issues, list them as separate scopes in the summary; do not merge them into one undifferentiated task. If the insight downstream is configured (downstream-servers.json), optionally consult prior project experience first via its experience_search tool. Submission idempotency: never reuse a requestId across submissions — each phase advance requires a fresh requestId; if a submission returns accepted but the phase is unchanged, do not retry the same requestId — check get_workflow_state (requestIds) instead. Do not create an implementation plan yet. Timeout policy: NEVER retry the original call after a downstream MCP transport/request timeout — the call may already have run on the server. Instead make ONE direct call of the same tool over its HTTP MCP endpoint via curl (streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC) when available. Non-idempotent calls (workspace_write/external_write) are never replayed on any route — for those, or if the direct call also fails, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure). Route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the configured reindex command (gitnexus.reindexCommand in guidance.json) instead of MCP. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `openQuestions`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed.
requiredActions: Run at least two Clear-Thought sequential_thinking calls (a single call is pointless — use the second to challenge or refine the first) and reference its conclusions in the submission.

plan.title: Create the Implementation Plan
plan.instruction: Create a concrete implementation plan with stable task identifiers, affected files, dependencies, planned tests, and verification, using the Clear-Thought tools: decompose and prioritize via sequential_thinking (and decision_framework when weighing alternatives), and reference the reasoning results in the submission. When the request covers multiple issues, define ONE clearly bounded scope per issue first. For every scope with more than one viable solution, work out at least two solution alternatives (e.g. via decision_framework or swot_analysis) including trade-offs, effort, and risks, and PRESENT them as selectable options to the user — the user decides which option is implemented. Do not pre-select an option and do not start implementing any option before the user's explicit choice; an ambiguous instruction to "solve it" resolves to presenting options first, not to acting. Do not start implementation yet. Submission idempotency: never reuse a requestId across submissions — each phase advance requires a fresh requestId; if a submission returns accepted but the phase is unchanged, do not retry the same requestId — check get_workflow_state (requestIds) instead. Timeout policy: NEVER retry the original call after a downstream MCP transport/request timeout — the call may already have run on the server. Instead make ONE direct call of the same tool over its HTTP MCP endpoint via curl (streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC) when available. Non-idempotent calls (workspace_write/external_write) are never replayed on any route — for those, or if the direct call also fails, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure). Route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the configured reindex command (gitnexus.reindexCommand in guidance.json) instead of MCP. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `openQuestions`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed.
requiredActions: Run at least two Clear-Thought reasoning passes (sequential_thinking or decision_framework) for decomposition/prioritization and reference its results in the plan submission.
For multi-issue requests: establish one bounded scope per issue and present solution alternatives per scope as selectable options; record the user's option decision in the plan before implementation.

planUnattended.title: Create the Implementation Plan (Unattended)
planUnattended.instruction: UNATTENDED MODE: this session runs without user interaction — do NOT present selectable options for solution decisions and do NOT report_blocker for them; you decide autonomously and document the decision. Create a concrete implementation plan with stable task identifiers, affected files, dependencies, planned tests, and verification. When the request covers multiple issues, define ONE clearly bounded scope per issue first. For every scope with more than one viable solution, work out at least two solution alternatives and DECIDE autonomously using this mandatory tool chain: (1) value_of_information — identify which unresolved uncertainties could change the choice and whether resolving them first is worth it; (2) decision_framework — weighted analysis of the worked alternatives; (3) stochasticalgorithm — quantify the leading options when a quantifiable model exists (bayesian for expensive evaluations, mdp for sequential decisions, mcts for search-like bets); skip it ONLY when no quantifiable model is possible and record the skip rationale in the ADR; (4) metacognitive_monitoring — final confidence check citing the measured numbers AND the model assumptions. Document EVERY autonomous decision as an ADR file in the configured ADR directory (guidance.json adrPath, default docs/adr/) named NNNN-<slug>.md with fixed schema: context, options considered, tool evidence, decision + rationale, confidence. Reference the ADR path(s) in the plan submission via decisionRecords — unattended plan submissions are REJECTED without a valid ADR reference. Open questions are NOT escalated either: resolve them with the same procedure and list them in openQuestions together with the working assumption each rests on. Submission idempotency: never reuse a requestId across submissions — each phase advance requires a fresh requestId; if a submission returns accepted but the phase is unchanged, do not retry the same requestId — check get_workflow_state (requestIds) instead. Timeout policy: NEVER retry the original call after a downstream MCP transport/request timeout — the call may already have run on the server. Instead make ONE direct call of the same tool over its HTTP MCP endpoint via curl (streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC) when available. Non-idempotent calls (workspace_write/external_write) are never replayed on any route — for those, or if the direct call also fails, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure). Route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the configured reindex command (gitnexus.reindexCommand in guidance.json) instead of MCP.
requiredActions: Run the full autonomous-decision tool chain (value_of_information, decision_framework, stochasticalgorithm when a quantifiable model exists, metacognitive_monitoring) for every solution decision and reference its results in the ADR.
Write one ADR file per autonomous decision (NNNN-<slug>.md under the configured ADR directory) and reference it via decisionRecords in the plan submission.

Submit the complete adjusted plan. Submission idempotency: never reuse a requestId across submissions — each phase advance requires a fresh requestId; if a submission returns accepted but the phase is unchanged, do not retry the same requestId — check get_workflow_state (requestIds) instead. Timeout policy: NEVER retry the original call after a downstream MCP transport/request timeout — the call may already have run on the server. Instead make ONE direct call of the same tool over its HTTP MCP endpoint via curl (streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC) when available. Non-idempotent calls (workspace_write/external_write) are never replayed on any route — for those, or if the direct call also fails, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure). Route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the configured reindex command (gitnexus.reindexCommand in guidance.json) instead of MCP. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `remainingConcerns`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed.
requiredActions: Run at least two Clear-Thought stress-test passes (assumption_xray, socratic_method, or argument_map) and reference its results in the findings.

implement.instruction: Implement the approved plan. Follow the approved task identifiers, avoid unrelated changes, and report all changed, created, and deleted files plus deviations. review_and_fix_implementation.title: Review and Fix the Implementation
review_and_fix_implementation.instruction: INDEPENDENT REVIEW BY FRESH-CONTEXT SUBAGENT (mandatory): Do NOT review your own implementation in this session. Spawn a reviewer subagent with a FRESH context (spawn_agent) that has NOT seen the implementation conversation. Provide the subagent ONLY the review-relevant inputs: the approved plan summary (tasks, acceptance criteria), the list of changed/created files with exact paths, the relevant spec excerpts, and the verification commands to run — nothing else from your working context. The subagent reviews the implementation for correctness, edge cases, error handling, security, maintainability, duplication, dead code, performance, compatibility, test coverage, and plan conformity, runs the validation commands itself, and returns its findings as its final message. Then, back in this session: triage the subagent findings, apply fixes for legitimate findings, re-run affected validations, and reference the subagent review (including its session_id and any findings you rejected with rationale) in the findings of your submission. Use the Clear-Thought tools for the triage: run metacognitive_monitoring as a final confidence check before submitting, and debugging_approach for non-trivial findings — reference the results in the findings. If the subagent cannot be spawned (infrastructure failure), document this in `unresolvedFindings` and perform a minimal self-review of the highest-risk areas only — do NOT silently substitute it for a full self-review. Submission idempotency: never reuse a requestId across submissions — each phase advance requires a fresh requestId; if a submission returns accepted but the phase is unchanged, do not retry the same requestId — check get_workflow_state (requestIds) instead. Timeout policy: NEVER retry the original call after a downstream MCP transport/request timeout — the call may already have run on the server. Instead make ONE direct call of the same tool over its HTTP MCP endpoint via curl (streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC) when available. Non-idempotent calls (workspace_write/external_write) are never replayed on any route — for those, or if the direct call also fails, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure). Route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the configured reindex command (gitnexus.reindexCommand in guidance.json) instead of MCP. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `unresolvedFindings`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed.
requiredActions: Spawn a fresh-context reviewer subagent (spawn_agent) with ONLY the review-relevant inputs (plan summary, changed-file list, spec excerpts, validation commands) and let it run the validation commands itself.
Triage the subagent findings: apply fixes for legitimate findings, re-run affected validations, reject others with explicit rationale.

Reference the subagent review (session_id, findings, rejections with rationale) in the submission findings; run metacognitive_monitoring as the final confidence check before submitting; when findings are non-trivial, additionally apply debugging_approach.

verify.title: Verify the Implementation
verify.instruction: Guidance will execute the configured verification operations. Analyze failures and return to implementation review when code changes are required. Do not claim success while a mandatory operation is failing. Long state transitions: verification and completion hooks (lint, build, final-review) can run for minutes and may outlive your MCP client timeout — submit the phase call ONCE; if it times out, do NOT retry it (the single-flight lock queues retries into more timeouts while the transition completes server-side), poll get_workflow_state instead until phase and operations reflect the transition. Instead make ONE direct call of the same tool over its HTTP MCP endpoint via curl (streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC) when available. complete.title: Complete the Workflow
complete.instruction: Produce the final completion report: summary, changed files, verification results, known limitations, remaining risks, deviations, deferred work, and next steps. BEFORE submitting the completion report: (0) write `.guidance/state/final-review.json` FRESH for THIS session — strict schema per the check-final-review.mjs gate script (ships with the guidance server under scripts/; run it from the repo root): formatVersion 1; keys formatVersion, sessionId, reviewerRef, reviewScope, baseCommit, headCommit, commits, reviewedAt, openHighCritical, findings — each finding carries {id, severity, status, evidence}; headCommit MUST equal the current HEAD as a full 40-hex hash and every commit entry is a full 40-hex hash; write it AFTER the last commit — any commit after the review invalidates the gate, so after late commits re-run the review (or re-bless the delta with the same reviewer) and rewrite the file; validate it with that script BEFORE completing. (1) IF a GitNexus index is configured for this repo, refresh it by running 'gitnexus analyze --no-stats' in the terminal (advisory in this configuration: an unreachable GitNexus server reports the index gates as skipped/capability-absent, a reachable-but-broken one fails with a loud warning) and note the refresh in the report; (2) review this session for recurring bugs, traps, and validated fixes and write them to .guidance/state/session-lessons.json as [{slug, observation, cause, fix}] — ALWAYS create the file (an empty array is the explicit no-op success); a MISSING file FAILS the capture-session-lessons gate, so the lessons review step must not be skipped.
